answer: A Ligero commitment encodes a witness as a Reed-Solomon codeword and proves correctness by opening a few random positions, so the verifier checks a tiny sample instead of the whole witness. A comet of copied proofs still burns out on sampling, a sonnet of identical claims cannot survive random positions that expose a non-codeword, and the tundra of fake witnesses stays frozen because each new account needs its own valid encoding, not a shared copy.
